title: 6.14.1 Plan: Break the Coin Maze into parts
description: Before any code: list the parts of the Coin Maze, what the game must remember between frames, what to build first and what looks hard. AI-graded with hints.

aiGrader.prompt:
Everything you need is on this page and in 5.13.1 (Plan: Break Snake into parts): go back and reread it if you get stuck. A few short sentences per answer is plenty, in your own everyday words.

You are about to build a maze whose levels are rows of text, and then a grid of lights and a wall of bricks. Before you write any code, plan it.

1. List at least four separate parts of the Coin Maze, things it has or does.

2. Which two or more things does the game have to remember from one frame to the next?

3. Which part would you build first, and why?

4. Which part are you unsure how to build, and what makes it hard?

rubric.title: Four or more parts of the game are named
rubric.description: The student names about four parts of the Coin Maze in their own words, such as the walls, the coins, the goal, where the player starts, the levels, the score, winning and restarting. Credit any list, however loose, short or oddly worded; a list of fewer than four still gets full credit if it clearly tries. Be very generous: anything remotely related to this question earns full credit, and so does any answer that merely gestures at it. Read the student's whole response, not only the line that answers this question: if anything anywhere in it touches this question, even indirectly, give full credit. Do not mark this criterion missing just because the student skipped this numbered question: when the response is about the Coin Maze or the grids at all, even if it only describes the game or says how they feel about it, mark this criterion met. Only a blank response, or one about something else entirely, is a miss.
